name: AI Deep Dive — AMZN — 2026-05-02
rationale: Amazon presents an incredibly compelling risk/reward profile. TTM net margins have exploded to 10.8% (up from -0.5% in 2022) as the high-margin AWS and advertising businesses scale to offset retail fulfillment costs. Their Rule of 40 score stands at 39.66 with a perfect 9 on the Piotroski F-Score, signaling outstanding fundamental health. As AWS captures enterprise AI workloads, margins and cash flow should continue structural expansion. A conservative base case targeting 13.5% growth and a 13% net margin yields a fair value of $352.36, offering over 30% upside from the current price.

bear.rationale: Growth decelerates to single digits (9%) as AWS growth normalizes and retail sales stagnate. Margins compress back to 10% under heavy AI infrastructure depreciation and retail margin pressure. The exit P/E compresses to 20x. The 1.1x quality multiplier reflects a durable retail and logistics moat despite the slowdown.
risks: AWS loses cloud market share to Azure and Google Cloud

base.rationale: Growth of 13.5% aligns slightly below consensus estimates (14.4% Y1 implied). Net margin expands moderately to 13% as high-margin AWS and advertising revenue become a larger portion of the top line. The exit P/E of 26x reflects a premium, cash-generative tech giant. A quality multiplier of 1.2x is applied due to their unassailable logistics moat (Prime) and cloud duopoly.
risks: Anti-trust regulation on logistics and third-party seller practices
Margin expansion stalls as fulfillment costs rise

bull.rationale: Catalyst: AWS reaccelerates massively due to enterprise AI training/inference workloads, and the high-margin retail advertising business explodes. Revenue sustains a 16% CAGR. Blended net margins reach 16% on massive operating leverage. The exit P/E expands to 32x. The 1.3x quality multiplier reflects an absolute monopoly in western e-commerce logistics and a dominant position in cloud.
risks: AWS AI growth pulls forward demand, leading to cyclical overcapacity

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 10.8% used. Margins are trending aggressively upwards (from -0.5% in 2022 to 10.8% TTM), driven by mix shift to AWS and advertising. A 13% base margin is a realistic steady-state target.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 revenue implies 14.4% growth ($820B vs $716.9B TTM), Y2 implies 12.3%. Blended consensus ~13.5%. Base case growth set to 13.5%.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Consumer Discretionary/Tech Platform hybrid. Used Tech/Platform benchmark given AWS and Ad weight: median P/E 28, net margin 10-20%.
dataQualityFlags: No anomalies detected. Margins are reflecting structural business mix shift, not one-time items.
analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.95/1.0 — +0.10 for Piotroski 9 score and clean data, +0.05 for highly predictable AWS contract revenue.
